# Common Ground Wiki

> Reference pages for Common Ground (also Common Ground Ventures), a principal-led group based in Phoenix, Arizona that builds, funds, operates, automates with AI and protects companies from the inside. Principals: Jesse Fowler, Alex Prince, Jimmy Khounlavong, Robby Prochnow, Nick Scavio. Every page here is created by Common Ground. Structured data on each page uses the organization id https://www.commonground.ventures/#org.

## About
- [Common Ground](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/common-ground/): the group, its five principals and its ventures
- [Results-Based Advisory](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/results-based-advisory/): how the group prices work, fee tied to a metric
- [Kinwork](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/kinwork/): the group's client tools (draft)
- [Data Rooms](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/data-rooms/): one data room per Common Ground project, indexed at https://datarooms.commonground.ventures/

## Principals
- [Jesse Fowler](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/jesse-fowler/)
- [Alex Prince](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/alex-prince/)
- [Jimmy Khounlavong](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/jimmy-khounlavong/)
- [Robby Prochnow](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/robert-prochnow/)
- [Nick Scavio](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/nick-scavio/)

## Ventures
- [Lïef Development + Construction](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/lief-development/): Luxury residential development and construction in Arizona; owner's representation, architecture, preconstruction and general contracting nationally through LÏEF Builders.
- [APEXX AI](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/apexx-ai/): AI automation agency; the group's AI deployment arm for small and mid-size businesses.
- [Lip Loi Creative](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/lip-loi-creative/): Brand strategy and go-to-market studio. Creating brands that fund.
- [Prince Capital](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/prince-capital/): Private investment advisory firm led by a registered representative.
- [Jasper Properties](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/jasper-properties/): Boutique short-term-rental management in Phoenix, Arizona.
- [Drive For The Dream](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/drive-for-the-dream/): Story-led golf sponsorship vehicle.
- [Romulus Entertainment](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/romulus-entertainment/): Feature-film production company; ten films across genres.
- [Bridgepoint Aviation](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/bridgepoint-aviation/): Private aviation advisory operating as BridgePoint Air Advisors.
- [Xtrata](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/xtrata/): Construction technology; the SABS composite building system.
- [Fluidmapper](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/fluidmapper/): Measured 3D flow data for industrial AI; Montreal.
- [Kinetic ML](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/kinetic-ml/): Concept-stage business-intelligence platform.
- [Chronicle News](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/chronicle-news/): Media venture; public footprint in development.
- [Plunge Studio](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/plunge-studio/): Hospitality venture held as a principal position.
- [Zen Aegis](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/zen-aegis/): AI transformation partner led by Robby Prochnow; builds and runs custom AI agent systems inside client businesses.
- [Tellus Design + Build](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/tellus-design-build/): prior firm, 2004 to 2023

## Work on record (64 engagements)
- [Index](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/)
- [A five-star barbershop](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/barbershop-client/): Website, a phone line of its own and booking into Square for a five-star barbershop, then planning for the owner's barber school franchise.
- [A&E Pre-Construction Partner](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/ae-preconstruction-partner/): Operating Partner to a national A&E pre-construction firm: a construction channel, 14 licensed architects and engineers sourced, and over $120 million in projects brought to bid.
- [Fluidmapper](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/fluidmapper/): How Fluidmapper measures three-dimensional flow inside opaque industrial vessels with radioactive particle tracking and AI reconstruction: the science, its history, the alternatives, four buyer groups and the limits.
- [Ground Truth Peptides](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/ground-truth-peptides/): A free, independent, evidence-graded reference for 42 research peptides built because honest information did not exist; sells nothing, takes no vendor money, and does not change a grade when the news changes.
- [Ground Control](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/health-vault/): A private health command center built because every consumer app optimizes for the platform that runs it; labs, imaging, genetics, training and protocols in one system the owner controls, hardened through five security rounds over 391 commits.
- [Jackie Allison, Newborn Care Specialist](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/jackie-allison-website/): A site and a cited, unambiguous search identity for an independent Newborn Care Specialist, live on her own domain three days after the ask.
- [Kanopi](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/kanopi-estimating-engine/): LÏEF's estimating engine, in place with eight builders and developers and over $600 million bid in 2026, publishing only the accuracy it earns blind.
- [Lip Loi Creative](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lip-loi-creative/): Common Ground's fractional CRO seat at Lip Loi Creative, a brand studio and Common Ground venture: fix it before you fund it, then bring the work in.
- [PC Analytics](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/pc-analytics/): A Prince Capital company that runs a practice group's growth as one program: off-market acquisitions, recruiting, data rooms, diligence and pipeline tracking.
- [PE-backed medical group](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/pe-backed-medical-group/): Fractional COO running a 90-day operations and efficiency audit for a PE-backed multi-office medical group: map first, govern second, build third.
- [Silver Mountain Ranches](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/silver-mountain-ranches/): A full Common Ground consulting engagement on a 344-acre Arizona homesite community: the model, the lender and investor case, the buyers, water and approvals, and the brand, reviewed the way the money will review it.
- [Trade Services Buy-Side Diligence](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/trade-services-buyside-diligence/): A live deal. Buy-side diligence for HighTide Capital Group: three tests, cheapest first. On the first target a $472,000 tax lookback surfaced before the earnings rebuild.
- [Aegis Lens](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/aegis-lens/): Aegis Lens is a Zen Aegis prototype that runs inside a client's environment, collects the facts a questionnaire would ask for, ranks what it finds with evidence and holds every deliverable for a person's approval.
- [Agent team for a multi-market business brokerage](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/brokerage-agent-team/): Five named agents on dedicated, isolated infrastructure took over inbox triage and buy-side origination for a multi-market business brokerage, reclaiming 71.3 inbox hours in seven days.
- [Alice Mushrooms](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/alice-mushrooms/): Seed go-to-market advice to a functional mushroom brand that reached 3,000-plus retail doors and the top item in its category at Sprouts and Target.
- [CRM Migration](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/crm-migration/): Moved Common Ground's relationship book off a marketing-funnel CRM onto a records-and-relationships CRM in one day, weeks after the first move.
- [Canyon Corporate](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/canyon-corporate/): A $2,041,596 partition package for Building 1 of a Phoenix office-to-residential conversion on Xtrata's SABS system; Building 2 priced the day its plans arrived.
- [Cascade IR](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/cascade-ir/): Within about a day of a posting for investor-deck automation, Zen Aegis built a working engine that refreshes approved investor decks in place from one data layer, with 46 fields wired to source and no change to the design.
- [Email operations that learn from corrections](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/email-operations-learning-loop/): An email triage system Zen Aegis runs for itself and for other organizations, where every human correction can become a permanent rule: 9,803 emails triaged from April to August 2026 and 34.7 hours a week reclaimed.
- [Expert program for an online education company](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/online-education-expert-program/): A complete expert program for an online education company, 17 modules and more than 80 lessons on a 10-week path, delivered live inside the first month.
- [Four apps in one day](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/four-apps-in-a-day/): Zen Aegis built four working apps live in a single day as a public demonstration, including a commercial insurance quoting tool and a credit intelligence tool, and separately had an autonomous agent build and compare two rapid-development platforms.
- [Foyer Hall](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/foyer-hall/): Foyer Hall is Zen Aegis's white-label client portal and data room. Common Ground moved its first client room onto it in late September 2026, and its first invoice became payable by bank or card on October 6.
- [Ghana Community](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/ghana-community/): Master plan and schematic design proposal for a new community in Ghana's Volta Region, with the building system and local crew training in scope.
- [Go-to-market build for a B2B SaaS company](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/b2b-saas-go-to-market-build/): Positioning, a new site, a blog system, four phases of search work, outreach and paid traffic for a B2B SaaS company, run as one retainer: 6,048 sessions in 130 days.
- [Grant Match AI](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/grant-match-ai/): A public, open-repository grant discovery engine for nonprofits that scores each funder on six factors, with rules doing the arithmetic and a model doing only the judgment calls.
- [Guardrails for a self-hosted agent platform](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/governed-agent-platform/): The controls Zen Aegis built into its own agent platform: a gate that blocks any AI claim without a live source, per-agent secrets, database-enforced tenancy, a ban on agents checking their own work, and a security memo client teams can review.
- [Hyatt Studios Georgetown](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/hyatt-studios-georgetown/): Feasibility study for a 122-key Hyatt Studios in Georgetown, Texas: an honest no in February, then a $9,572,784 estimate the developer is raising against.
- [Jason Scott](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/jason-scott-luxury-apparel/): Go-to-market and raise advisory for a luxury menswear brand: the plan rebuilt from the door up showed a $7 million raise would run dry in year three.
- [Lifted Trucks mission control](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lifted-trucks-mission-control/): A collective Common Ground proof of concept for Lifted Trucks, a prospective client: a working six-screen demo of what a mission control for multi-state inventory could look like, shipped May 21, 2026.
- [Medical device US entry](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/medical-device-us-entry/): Diligence, a data room and a go-to-market plan for an Irish medical-device company's US entry; five findings surfaced before any investor saw a page.
- [Medical-record review for an in-house legal team](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/legal-team-medical-record-review/): Zen Aegis automated the gathering, summarizing and delivery of medical records for an in-house legal team; one case that historically cost about $75,000 came in at a fraction of the cost in one-tenth of the time.
- [Modular fabrication center](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/modular-fabrication-center/): An initial business-model analysis for an Arizona modular housing plant: a stage-gated pipeline, a paid feasibility gate and schedule-first pricing.
- [Nevada multifamily value engineering](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/multifamily-204-units/): A budgetary comparison on a 204-unit Nevada multifamily: $154.70 a square foot on a structural panel system against a $167.50 stick-framed midpoint, on identical scope.
- [Search build for an independent financial advisory practice](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/financial-advisory-search-build/): A publishing system and a local landing page for an independent financial advisory practice ranked second in organic search for a competitive metro retirement-planning keyword within the first week, with no ad spend.
- [Sites for a strategy firm, a youth sports nonprofit and a family foundation](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/three-client-site-builds/): Three live client builds: a rebuilt homepage and development standard for a strategy consulting firm, a site with online registration for a youth sports nonprofit, and a hosted site for a family foundation.
- [Slipstream scoring engine](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/slipstream-scoring-engine/): Slipstream's automated engine scores how a site shows up in search and AI answers. Before it was trusted it was run against an expert's hand audit of ten sites and agreed 92.8 percent of the time with no factual conflicts.
- [The Triangle Grand Avenue](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/the-triangle-grand-avenue/): Development lead for a Phoenix broker group on a Grand Avenue creative district: feasibility, parcel research, a consortium pledge and capital last.
- [HighTide Capital](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/hightide-capital/): Operations and integration seat at an Arizona trade-services buy-and-build platform: a written buy box, broker mandates, a financing log and a close date.
- [HighTide Desk Tools](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/hightide-desk-tools/): A base-rate tracker, a liability-search checklist, an earnings bridge and an offer-structure method that every HighTide target runs through in order.
- [Xtrata](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/xtrata-sabs-consulting-seat/): Fractional CRO and construction consultant to Xtrata: $48 million of projects bid, a $220 million pipeline, a bid system of record and a parity pitch.
- [BridgePoint Air](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/bridgepoint-air/): Advisory board seat at a private aviation advisory firm from formation through its sale to a much larger private aviation company in November 2025; the reframe doubled the offer.
- [Drive for the Dream](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/drive-for-the-dream/): A docuseries on developmental golfers chasing a tour card: eight golfers and three producing partners signed first, then a move to sponsorship the venture controls.
- [301 W Osborn](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lief-midtown-301-osborn/): LÏEF's own conversion of a 1971 Midtown Phoenix office tower, bought for $3.85M, into 22 condominiums, with the permit path locked before the unit count.
- [Phoenix short-term rental launch](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/property-management-launch/): Advisor on the business model and launch of a boutique short-term rental management company in Phoenix: one flat fee and the controls it needs.
- [Aycre Capital](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/aycre-capital-fund/): Managing Director of a Las Vegas custom-home fund: sequenced the ask, built a staged pipeline and reached $25M in commitments toward a $50M target.
- [Lip Loi Creative portfolio](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lip-loi-studio-work/): Brand identities and decks Lip Loi Creative built under Common Ground's direction, for athletes, a golf venture, a developer and a deep-tech company.
- [Greensleeves Steakhouse](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/greensleeves-steakhouse/): Took over a dark 1892 Redlands landmark for effectively nothing, extended the lease first, rebuilt it around live service, kept it open through COVID, exited in 2022.
- [Ritz-Carlton Laguna Beach](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/ritz-carlton-laguna-beach/): Two narrow Tellus-era credits: an outdoor patio built for the Ritz-Carlton in Laguna Beach and development advisory on Ritz-Carlton branded residences.
- [Village San Juan](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/village-san-juan/): Tellus Management kept a 446-unit community's maintenance and emergency contract on a board vote and ran it for seven years.
- [Ink Games](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/ink-games/): Seed Advisor, Go-to-Market, for an Austin mobile-gaming studio before its first title: the pitch moved onto the team, and the seed closed in 2020.
- [Santa Monica house](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/santa-monica-house/): Tellus finished a custom Santa Monica home in 2020 after the crews stopped coming, sorting open work by license or skill and doing the skilled work itself.
- [AXT Axe Haus](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/axt-axe-haus/): Southern California's first axe-throwing venue: proved it live, won Costa Mesa's first use permit for the category, and holds on as a long-term play.
- [LA Clippers Practice Facility](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/la-clippers-practice-facility/): Tellus designed and rebuilt the Clippers' practice facility room by room, in phases, with the team in the building the whole way through.
- [LACMA](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lacma-sculpture/): Tellus Build fabricated and installed an artist's interactive sculpture at LACMA, inside a two-year volunteer owner's representative seat on campus art.
- [Carroll Shelby International, Gardena](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/carroll-shelby-gardena/): Tellus built Carroll Shelby International's California hub in four phases over four years and won an exemption from Carson's construction freeze.
- [Contractor Gorilla](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/contractor-gorilla/): Advisor with an equity position in Contractor Gorilla, a Los Angeles agency for contractors; wrote the search plan that held Tellus on Google's page one for years.
- [Soft-Story Retrofits](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/soft-story-retrofit/): Tellus launched a seismic retrofit line for Los Angeles's mandatory ordinance, with PACE financing and a structural engineer inside one offer.
- [Habitat for Humanity](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/habitat-for-humanity/): A construction partner to Habitat chapters in three Southern California counties for nearly a decade, shifting from surplus material to labor and bid work.
- [H.E.E.A.L. Santa Barbara](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/heeal-santa-barbara/): Volunteer president of a Santa Barbara grief and loss nonprofit, building its outreach, fundraising and board governance around the people who refer families.
- [Shelby American Las Vegas](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/shelby-american-las-vegas/): Owner's rep and construction manager for Shelby American's Las Vegas move, run trade-direct where Tellus held no license; opened on schedule in March 2015.
- [Sublime Medical](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/sublime-medical/): Fractional COO for a three-practice dermatology group: traced a collections problem to stale billing codes, and insurance billing rose 42 percent.
- [Save the World Air](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/save-the-world-air/): A consulting seat at a small public pipeline-flow technology company in Santa Barbara, around 2011: testing a hard claim from close range.
- [Greensburg, Kansas](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/greensburg-kansas/): After an EF5 tornado, national supplier partnerships sold as on-camera category slots delivered more than $30 million in donated green materials.
- [Surrogacy Consulting Startup](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/surrogacy-consulting-startup/): Advised an unnamed surrogacy startup on its first customer, a state-by-state rollout, and where AI can cut surrogacy and IVF paperwork costs.

## Work on record, Jimmy Khounlavong (117 pages)
- [301 West Osborn rollout plan: the rewrite from version 1 to version 2](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lief-osborn-rollout-plan-v2/): Khounlavong reviewed his partner's marketing rollout plan for 301 West Osborn and produced version 2.0, which added the brand architecture, replaced the buyer profile and set a two-voice content plan.
- [Brand standards: six files that partners and their agents read](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/brand-standards-for-six-brands/): Khounlavong wrote and owns one brand standard per brand, for six brands, so that partners and their AI agents draw every visual decision from the same source.
- [Content system: a posting plan for the group's brands that stayed mostly internal](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/content-system/): Khounlavong set the cadence, the channel rules and the templates for posting across the Common Ground brands. The system was built and largely did not publish.
- [Drive for the Dream: a show brand built before the show](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/drive-for-the-dream-brand/): Khounlavong built the identity, the player color system and the investor-facing content plan for a golf docuseries that is not yet placed with a platform. The show was conceived by Jesse Fowler and Hunter Schwartz, and Khounlavong was in it from the beginning.
- [Fluidmapper: a brand system and a site for a deep-tech measurement company](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/fluidmapper-brand-and-site/): Khounlavong built the Fluidmapper brand system, designed and built fluidmapper.com, and produced its conference and sales materials. His partner Jesse Fowler leads the client relationship.
- [Fluidmapper datasets gate: sample data behind a short form](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/fluidmapper-datasets-gate/): Khounlavong built a gated download page on fluidmapper.com that trades a sample data package for a name, an email and a stated purpose, and tells the sales inbox who took what.
- [Jason Scott: a buy plan built from the unit up for a luxury menswear brand](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/jason-scott-buy-plan/): Khounlavong built the merchandising buy plan for Jason Scott, a luxury menswear brand before launch. His partner Jesse Fowler ran the client relationship, built the data rooms, set the brand up with a vendor for the purchase order, and held the capital work with Prince Capital; go-to-market was shared. The engagement paused in July 2026.
- [Lïef Development company brand: the identity, a 13-week content program and two company sites](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lief-development-company-brand-and-sites/): Khounlavong set the company identity for Lïef Development, planned its LinkedIn content program, and did the search and AI readiness work on the two company sites.
- [Lïef Midtown plan set: a compiled drawing set, re-presented in the project brand and gated](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lief-midtown-plan-set-review/): Khounlavong took the compiled plan set for Lïef Midtown, set its type and callouts to the project brand, and moved it behind a gate on the project domain for consultants and capital partners.
- [Lïef Midtown residence pages: 22 homes on one template, readable by search and AI engines](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lief-midtown-residence-pages-and-search-readiness/): Khounlavong rebuilt the 22 residence pages from one data file and one template, then had each page written out in full so that search and AI engines can read it.
- [Lïef Midtown selections: three tiers, three design levels and a 109-page look-book](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lief-selections-program-and-look-book/): Khounlavong turned a single finish board into a selections program of three tiers by three design levels, and published it as a 109-page look-book on the buyer site.
- [Lïef Osborn investor deck: the brand and buyer narrative inside a shared document](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lief-osborn-investor-deck-narrative/): Khounlavong built the brand system the investor deck uses, wrote its buyer narrative and did a first pass on the deck, then worked on it with his partner Jesse Fowler.
- [Lïef two-brand system: one company brand, one project brand, and a rule for which to use](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lief-two-brand-visual-system/): Khounlavong split Lïef into a company brand for the industry and a project brand for home buyers, and wrote the standard that governs both.
- [Principal sites: five personal sites on one shared pattern](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/principal-sites/): Khounlavong built or rebuilt the personal sites of all five Common Ground principals, on one shared structure, and put two of them live on Common Ground subdomains.
- [Search and AI readiness: the Common Ground standard for sites that search engines and AI answer engines can read](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/search-and-ai-readiness/): Search and AI readiness is the Common Ground standard for making its sites readable to search engines and AI answer engines. Khounlavong wrote the audit method, put the first layer on the sites he controls from April 2026, and graded and fixed the sites by hand. Jesse Fowler was in it early and requested the July 2026 audit.
- [The Fundable Founder's Playbook and Fundability Score: the studio's method, sold as a product](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/fundable-founders-playbook-and-score/): Khounlavong turned Lip Loi Creative's two-phase method into a free scored assessment and a 73-page workbook, and his own file records no Playbook sales by April 17, 2026.
- [Work and seat map: every company on one map, by the seat the group held](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/work-and-seat-map/): Khounlavong set the seat taxonomy for a map of 33 companies on the rebuilt Common Ground site. The rebuilt site is on staging. It is not live.
- [commonground.ventures: the group's site, restructured section by section in 2026](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/commonground-ventures-site/): Khounlavong built and ran the Common Ground site through 2026. He holds 71 of the 72 commits on its main branch, and the other one is his own agent's.
- [liefmidtownphx.com: a buyer site rebuilt to the project brand and opened to search](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lief-midtown-website-rebuild-and-launch/): Khounlavong rebuilt the Lïef Midtown buyer site to the project brand standard, launched it on its own domain on June 25, 2026, and opened it to search engines on July 1, 2026.
- [SQAIRZ: a line plan and brand diagnostic for a golf footwear brand's pickleball business](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/sqairz-pickleball-brand-and-product-scope/): A golf footwear brand already in pickleball, with its first pickleball shoe in market and its second in development, had real technology and no settled view of who the shoe was for or what the brand stood for in the sport. Khounlavong wrote a four-pillar scope of work and built the diagnostic that put the consumer first, made the case for showing the technology, and drew the tools a more robust line plan runs on, to SQAIRZ's own models and prices.
- [The Negotiated Apology Project: brand guidelines for a conflict resolution practice](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/negotiated-apology-project-brand-guidelines/): Khounlavong wrote the brand guidelines, redrew the logo and rebuilt the client's talk as a branded presentation between December 2024 and April 2025.
- [Lïef Midtown: a building is a product, and this one became a brand](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lief-midtown-brand-system/): Brand architecture for the adaptive reuse of a 1971 Midtown Phoenix office building into 22 residences, from naming and identity through the buyer experience and a three-tier selections program.
- [Aycre Capital: the brand and the deck behind a custom-home fund](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/aycre-brand-and-narrative/): Khounlavong built the brand guidelines, carried the investor deck through 15 saved versions and drew three community brands for a Las Vegas fund that did not close near its target.
- [Kinetic ML: a pitch deck for sports science, not yet in market](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/kinetic-ml-pitch-deck/): Khounlavong built the pitch deck for a sports science and prediction venture across four versions, from a golf pitch in November 2023 to an all-sports pitch in April 2024. The venture has not gone to market.
- [Luke Kwon: a brand system built from scratch, and a client who chose another route](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/luke-kwon-brand-system/): Khounlavong built a brand strategy, an identity and a sponsor pitch deck for a golf creator in early 2024. It was presented, and the client chose another route.
- [Vincent Hancock: a brand for the person behind the medals](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/vincent-hancock-brand-system/): Khounlavong ran discovery with the Olympic skeet champion, wrote the positioning and built the identity through three versions between July and October 2024.
- [Jasper Brands: a golf polo line built to launch with a show](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/jasper-brands-golf-polo-line/): Khounlavong wrote the product and brand brief for a golf apparel line built to give the unsigned golfers of Drive for the Dream an apparel deal, and to launch with the show. The brief runs from the faults of the standard polo to a nine-item assortment and a production calendar.

- [Iconic: the brief that gave a sneaker boutique its first mall door](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/iconic-mall-positioning-deck/): A sneaker boutique was about to take its first mall location and needed to know what it stood for. In two days Khounlavong gave it a position, a customer, an assortment and a store format it could take to landlords and backers.
- [No Caller ID: a voice and a design language for a Los Angeles consultancy](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/no-caller-id-voice-and-design-language/): Khounlavong curated the voice and the design language of the No Caller ID website, and built brand strategy and deck templates for some of its clients. The work came before Lip Loi Creative was a business and was the reason he started it.

- [One city, three businesses, one calendar: how Los Angeles set and shaped Nike's launches](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/los-angeles-launch-calendar/): Khounlavong set the Los Angeles calendar of events around each drop, influenced launch timing with Nike's global and North America teams, and worked in concert with Nike Basketball and Jordan Brand so that drops built toward the city's biggest sport and entertainment moments.

He did not lead the city plan.

- [Running channel briefs: product written for where the consumer shops](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/running-channel-briefs/): In Men's Running, Khounlavong asked Nike's global product team for colors and packs made for single channels and single accounts, each with a reason, a flow date and a forecast.

- [Sell-through expectations by launch tier: 90 days, 45 days, 14 days, 1 day](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/sell-through-expectations-by-launch-tier/): Khounlavong gave every shoe in the North America men's running line a planned sell-through window, set by its role in the line and by the channel it was sold in.
- [Spring 2018: $66.0M of gaps, $60.2M of requests](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/spring-2018-gap-closing/): When the spring 2018 men's running line came back from Nike's global review gate 17.8% under target, Khounlavong itemized every gap and built the product, color and pack requests to close it.
- [The master visual line plan: a retailer friendly template, adopted across categories](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/master-visual-line-plan-template/): Khounlavong rebuilt the seasonal line plan for North America men's running footwear so that sales teams and retailers could read it, and the template was taken up by other categories.

Khounlavong drove it at account level, rewriting the internal material into versions that Finish Line, the city specialty accounts, Shoe Palace and Hibbett Sports could use.

- [Hibbett Sports: a door cluster framework built on the retailer's own three store types](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/hibbett-sports-door-clusters/): Khounlavong told Hibbett Sports that with three consumer types it was in essence three different companies, then built Nike's assortment plan around the three profiles the retailer had already defined.

- [The Zoom Soldier: a shoe the athlete can be proud to wear, at any income](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/zoom-soldier-x/): Held LeBron's accessible tier at $125 to $130 under a $200 game shoe, and re-imagined the franchise for its tenth year around his true fans.
- [Athlete focus groups: what 17 year old players told the footwear team](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/athlete-focus-groups-2014-2015/): Across three market trips in 2014 and 2015, Khounlavong led the footwear part of focus groups with high school and club players in Las Vegas, Los Angeles and Chicago, and wrote up what they said about price, technology and the Hyper line.
- [Conquer the Core: a plan for every basketball shoe under $120](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/conquer-the-core/): Khounlavong led a strategy for the lower priced half of North America Basketball footwear in 2015, after three years in which signature shoes grew and everything under $100 shrank.
- [Fiscal 2015: plan beaten every season as the market turned](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/fiscal-2015-plan-beaten-every-season/): In his last full year in Basketball, Khounlavong's footwear business beat its plan in all four seasons and passed $500M for the first time, while he recorded that growth was slowing and began the work of a reset.
- [Margin tools: reading the price ladder before the season was bought](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/margin-tools-and-price-ladder/): Khounlavong built a gross margin evaluation template in his first merchandising year, grew it into a blended margin calculation tool, and used it in seasonal margin reviews that moved prices and forecasts toward the models that earned more.
- [Net Collectors Society: a March Madness brief that became a pack](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/net-collectors-society-march-madness/): Khounlavong wrote the spring 2015 March Madness brief, titled "What The Madness", pioneered the Net Collectors Society pack that came out of it, and planned the pack's second spring before he left the category.
- [Nike Basketball, North America: four signature franchises on one roadmap](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/nike-basketball-north-america/): Owned the four-year roadmap for North America Basketball footwear through the Kobe, LeBron, KD and Kyrie years. The business grew from $322M to $670M and passed $500M for the first time.
- [Nike Factory Store basketball: planning the second life of each shoe](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/nike-factory-store-basketball-program/): Khounlavong built a working rhythm with the Nike Factory Store buying team from his first merchandising year, mapped which basketball models would move into factory stores and when, and saw the channel's basketball footwear grow 9% in spring 2015.
- [Signature 2.0: resetting a business that had outrun its consumer](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/signature-2-0/): After four years of growth, signature basketball sell-through was slowing as prices rose. He wrote the five-step reset, and a companion plan for everything under $120.
- [Signature Launch Calendar: one page that ran the launch business for four years](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/signature-launch-calendar/): Khounlavong built a launch calendar for signature basketball footwear in October 2011 and kept it current through 72 versions, until the week he handed the category over in October 2015.
- [Signature Playbook: one version of the truth for every launch](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/signature-playbook-and-moments-line-plan/): Khounlavong conceived the Signature Playbook, a single shared tool and a Monday meeting that consolidated the tools each function used, and developed a visual line plan organized around sport, retail and brand moments.
- [Sporting goods strategy: three days in Dallas stores, then a plan for five accounts](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/sporting-goods-strategy-and-dallas-trip/): Khounlavong captained the footwear team on a January 2015 market trip to Dallas, then wrote the footwear case for making Nike Basketball a year round destination in sporting goods.
- [The Kill Zone: growing the mid price band under signature](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/kill-zone-mid-price-footwear/): Khounlavong made the mid price band of performance basketball footwear a stated goal in fiscal 2013 and grew it 31% that year, then kept asking product teams to fill the band as signature prices climbed above it.
- [Three year line plan: a standing plan for what to sell, at what price, in which season](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/three-year-line-plan/): Khounlavong created the three year line plan framework for North America Basketball in November 2013 and kept it as a working document through at least twelve versions, until he left the category in 2015.
- [Amplify Basketball: performance and sportswear sold to retailers as one story](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/amplify-basketball-and-basketball-by-nike/): Khounlavong co-led the Amplify Basketball work for North America with his Nike Sportswear counterpart, and in fiscal 2013 piloted "Basketball by Nike", a single cross category assortment and message, with key retailers.
- [Fiscal 2014: 17% growth on flat inventory](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/fiscal-2014-growth-with-flat-inventory/): In fiscal 2014 Khounlavong grew North America Basketball footwear revenue 17.1%, raised gross margin 230 basis points, held inventory flat and cut the cancel rate by a third.
- [Air Visi Pro III: a $65 shoe at the top of the October 2012 sales chart](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/air-visi-pro-iii/): In his first merchandising year Khounlavong influenced Nike's global product team on the Air Visi Pro III, an entry price basketball shoe, and in October 2012 it was the top selling performance basketball model in the United States by retail dollars.
- [Fiscal 2013: share, margin and fewer styles in the same year](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/fiscal-2013-share-margin-fewer-styles/): In his second year as the footwear merchant for North America Basketball, Khounlavong grew footwear revenue 15%, raised margin and market share, and did it with fewer styles than the year before.
- [LeBron X: a holiday 2012 launch planned colorway by colorway](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/lebron-x-launch-holiday-2012/): Khounlavong held the footwear merchandising seat for the LeBron X launch in holiday 2012, planned it by colorway on his launch calendar, and wrote a quick strike brief that sized the season at 30% above the year before.
- [Los Angeles Sales: All-Star, Kobe and the two retailers who owned the city](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/los-angeles-first-tour/): Lead Nike Sportswear representative in the second largest market in the country, carrying Shiekh and WSS through a championship year and the 2011 All-Star Game.
- [NBA All-Star 2011 in Los Angeles: the distribution plan, door by door](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/all-star-2011-los-angeles-distribution-plan/): Khounlavong built the West Territory's product distribution plan for the 2011 NBA All-Star Game in Los Angeles, and boutique sell-through averaged 67.4% across nine doors.

- [WSS: a three-year plan for the street retailer serving Hispanic Los Angeles](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/wss-three-year-plan/): Khounlavong wrote the fiscal 2012 to 2014 plan for WSS, asked Nike to raise the level of its best doors, and tied a South Gate homecoming event back to the stores.

- [Next Urban Gear: a three-year plan to reposition a Cleveland retailer](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/next-urban-gear-account-plans/): Khounlavong wrote a strategic plan for Next Urban Gear in Ohio, one of four account plans he wrote and communicated in fiscal 2010.
- [Six Points, Chicago: a Nike energy space built with a retailer](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/six-points-chicago/): As the boutique account executive in Chicago, led the commerce and marketplace side of Six Points, the Central Region's first Nike energy space, opened with St. Alfred for the 2010 World Cup.
- [Three new boutique doors: Phenom, Pogo and Haberdash](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/new-boutique-doors-phenom-pogo-haberdash/): Khounlavong opened Phenom in Minneapolis and Pogo outside Detroit, and filed to open Haberdash in Chicago, each to fill a gap he had found in the market.
- [Dunham's football cleats: from 45% share to 65%](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/dunhams-football-cleat-share/): Khounlavong took Nike's share of football cleats at Dunham's from 45% in July 2006 to 65% by fiscal 2009, and read Under Armour's arrival in the category from the shelf.
- [Electronic ordering: two sporting goods chains moved off hand-keyed orders](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/electronic-ordering-mc-sports-dunhams/): Khounlavong moved MC Sports and Dunham's onto electronic order entry, Nike.net and shared retail data, after starting the same work with his first accounts in 2004.
- [MC Sports: a shared stock to sales plan that became common practice](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/mc-sports-shared-stock-to-sales-plan/): Khounlavong built a stock to sales plan with MC Sports, got the retailer to share its numbers on a schedule, and made joint planning the way the account was run.
- [MC Sports team basketball: a team program for a retailer that had never run one](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/mc-sports-team-basketball-program/): Khounlavong proposed a team basketball program to MC Sports, a retailer that was losing the business to local team dealers, and grew it season over season.
- [Midwest Sporting Goods retailers: mutual stock-to-sales plans with two chains](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/detroit-sporting-goods/): Eight months into Nike, took the lead seat on MC Sports and Dunham's, two of the Central territory's largest sporting goods accounts, and built mutual stock-to-sales plans with both, so the seasonal buys came from a plan the retailer and Nike had made together.
- [The Football Planning Tool: planning forms that buyers and other reps picked up](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/football-planning-tool/): Khounlavong wrote a category planning workbook for football with a user guide for other reps, and built the seasonal forms that the Dunham's buyers came to plan from.
- [Asian American Heritage Month: an open house for Nike's Central region](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/asian-american-heritage-month-open-house/): Khounlavong led the team that staged an Asian American Heritage Month open house at Nike's Chicago showroom in May 2007, and hosted it from the stage.
- [Joga Bonito in Michigan: futsal events read for the retailer](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/joga-bonito-futsal-michigan/): Khounlavong worked the Joga Bonito futsal events staged with Dunham's and MC Sports in spring 2006, and turned them into a recap of who came, what they tried on and what it meant for each account.
- [The Hot Bag and Quick Facts mailers: retail math and accessories, sold by post](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/hot-bag-and-quick-facts-mailers/): In his first year at Nike, Khounlavong used mailers to teach retail math to his retailers and to sell accessories into Cleveland, and recorded the result against his own goal.
- [CDW: 125 accounts and a $15M book in Chicago](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/cdw/): Between Medline and Nike, Khounlavong sold technology for CDW in Chicago, carrying 125 accounts and more than $15M in revenue, up 5% on the prior year.
- [Medline: contract adoption and a pain management plan across 18 hospitals](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/medline-baptist-hospital-system/): Before Nike, Khounlavong sold medical supplies to an 18-facility hospital system from Memphis, and produced two separate results: $20M through contract adoption and about 11% growth through a pain management plan.
- [The Finish Line: a store grown from $3M to $5M](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/work/finish-line-lexington-store/): Khounlavong started at The Finish Line at 16, became an assistant manager in Lexington, and helped grow annual store volume from $3M to $5M.

- [Banning round numbers from the bid](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/banning-round-numbers-from-the-bid/): A residential bid needed a defensible price per square foot story, and the fast, simple math, total price divided by livable square footage, was spitting out a number that felt too low and wouldn't hold up next to a comp

- [Bringing design in house to own the schedule, not to sell design](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/bringing-design-in-house-to-own-the-schedule-not-to-sell-design/): Tellus started as a plan expediting service, run at a loss, aimed at making permit approvals predictable.
- [Building the bench instead of doing it alone](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/building-the-bench-instead-of-doing-it-alone/): After nineteen years running Tellus mostly by myself across every function, I started what became Common Ground Ventures.
- [Building the estimating algorithm a decade before AI could do it](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/building-the-estimating-algorithm-a-decade-before-ai-could-do-it/): Every trade prices its work off a repeatable metric, room count, linear feet, square feet, but the standard industry process was to send drawings out to trades and wait weeks for bids to come back.
- [Building the product he needed, at a loss](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/building-the-product-he-needed-at-a-loss/): Operating from San Diego to Santa Barbara, Tellus had no reliable way to forecast when a project would actually clear a city's permitting process.
- [Cutting The Fleet Down To What Actually Earns Its Keep](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/cutting-the-fleet-down-to-what-actually-earns-its-keep/): By mid-2026 I'd built a wide fleet of scheduled AI routines, briefings, outreach, content, audits.
- [Cutting the Cheap Number Even Though It Sounded Good](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/cutting-the-cheap-number-even-though-it-sounded-good/): A draft of the new Common Ground website described the four principals as having '100+ years collective' experience, and led with a headline claiming they were 'the only ones' who could do all three of the firm's lanes a
- [Graduated Trust After A Real Mistake](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/graduated-trust-after-a-real-mistake/): I wanted automated help scouting and drafting LinkedIn comments in my own voice.
- [Hearing the bigger business hiding behind the pitch](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/hearing-the-bigger-business-hiding-behind-the-pitch/): A mattress topper founder pitched me and a partner.
- [I Already Paid For These Mistakes, You Don't Have To](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/i-already-paid-for-these-mistakes-you-dont-have-to/): When a partner stood up a new shared operating stack for the whole company, I ran my own migration onto it first, before my other two partners touched theirs.
- [I sent the bid flawed on purpose](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/i-sent-the-bid-flawed-on-purpose/): An analysis flagged me for shipping a takeoff with known issues to another bidder, reading it as a failure of my own verification rule.
- [Is that the problem or the solution?](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/is-that-the-problem-or-the-solution/): A plan to make me findable by AI models treated my many concurrent company affiliations as an entity resolution problem, too many names attached to one person, to be trimmed down so a model could pin me down.
- [Make the check repeatable before the content](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/make-the-check-repeatable-before-the-content/): Our first prospect data room was built decision by decision: folders, access, layout, write-up style.
- [Mapping the process before automating it, for a client seven states wide](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/mapping-the-process-before-automating-it-for-a-client-seven-states-wid/): Construction estimating across my own companies traditionally took about six weeks per job.
- [Naming The Gap Instead Of Hiding It](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/naming-the-gap-instead-of-hiding-it/): Bidding as construction manager on a public affordable housing project in Santa Cruz County, my firm had real relevant experience but a genuine gap: no direct track record with that county or with a public housing author
- [Naming the credibility gap out loud](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/naming-the-credibility-gap-out-loud/): With Tellus, we sat on the first page of Google for ten years, and I never had to think twice about whether people believed our track record was real.
- [Nobody was really buying green](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/nobody-was-really-buying-green/): My first client at Tellus cared, more than any client I had met, about what she would be breathing and touching inside her own house.
- [Our own record does not get to be shy about our own work](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/our-own-record-does-not-get-to-be-shy-about-our-own-work/): The partners' copy of the wins ledger went out with every acquisition row stripped from it.
- [Pricing the tradeoff of being fast, with his eyes open](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/pricing-the-tradeoff-of-being-fast-with-his-eyes-open/): Once Tellus could turn around a detailed, well reasoned estimate in two days instead of the standard three weeks, a new risk showed up.
- [Refusing to sell a negotiating budget as an engineered certainty](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/refusing-to-sell-a-negotiating-budget-as-an-engineered-certainty/): A landowner needed a road cost figure to underwrite a lot purchase negotiation.
- [Sound pods first, soundproofing when they asked](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/sound-pods-first-soundproofing-when-they-asked/): Keller Williams wanted a roughly 5,000 square foot LA office near LAX, mostly open community space.
- [Style is countable: measuring my own voice before letting agents use it](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/style-is-countable-measuring-my-own-voice-before-letting-agents-use-it/): Copy written by agents was going out under the partners' names and reading like a machine.
- [Taking Tellus Design at a loss to control the timeline](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/taking-tellus-design-at-a-loss-to-control-the-timeline/): Early in Tellus I made a call that looked wrong on paper.
- [Telling a friend his dream house cost six to twelve million more than the market would pay back](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/telling-a-friend-his-dream-house-cost-six-to-twelve-million-more-than/): A personal friend asked me to help a couple navigate their general contractor's budget on a custom mountain home, at a schematic design stage where the vertical construction alone was pricing well above comparable homes 
- [Telling prospects the email was written by an AI](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/telling-prospects-the-email-was-written-by-an-ai/): Third party outreach tools were clunky and unreliable, so we replaced them with a custom AI and scheduled tasks system.
- [The 2 a.m. tell](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/the-2-a-m-tell/): I was weighing a significant career opportunity and needed a way to separate real conviction from talking myself into something that looked good on paper.
- [The Fourteen-Day Rule](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/the-fourteen-day-rule/): The old system let to-do items quietly auto-archive after seven days.
- [The Machine I Thought Was Idle Was The One On Fire](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/the-machine-i-thought-was-idle-was-the-one-on-fire/): I run my own work plus a growing fleet of scheduled AI tasks across three machines and two separate subscription plans, and I had a clear mental model of which plan carried which machine's load.
- [The domain was burned, and nobody had said it out loud](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/the-domain-was-burned-and-nobody-had-said-it-out-loud/): Outbound email was bouncing across multiple inboxes, drafts were quietly disappearing, and the team kept running campaigns and tweaking messages like the problem was the writing.
- [The keyhole](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/the-keyhole/): Asked how much of his history was ready to ship, the system reported roughly twenty engagements with usable backup.
- [The macro numbers go](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/the-macro-numbers-go/): A week of ledger work went into reconciling career totals.
- [The nine-month method](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/the-nine-month-method/): I left college on purpose, no plan anyone around me would've called sensible.
- [The overnight blitz that corrupted its own proof](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/the-overnight-blitz-that-corrupted-its-own-proof/): I ran a certification blitz overnight across two machines.
- [The speed camera at the stoplight](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/the-speed-camera-at-the-stoplight/): Clients regularly asked me why they should pay for an owner's representative on top of a general contractor they already trusted.
- [Trust the trend, not the point](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/trust-the-trend-not-the-point/): An Oura ring and an Apple Watch report the same body differently, and the ring throws outliers that are just wrong.
- [Two brands, two speeds](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/two-brands-two-speeds/): We were running two very different offers under one roof.
- [Two words and four months of notice](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/two-words-and-four-months-of-notice/): Someone close to me was taking a green interior design course, and one class handed her two words that changed my career path before the night was over.
- [Vertically integrating so nobody could point fingers but him](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/vertically-integrating-so-nobody-could-point-fingers-but-him/): I started Tellus in 2004 as a green construction company.
- [Walking away from a deal that kept changing its own numbers](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/walking-away-from-a-deal-that-kept-changing-its-own-numbers/): A longtime architect relationship, Brian Fracasse, forwarded me a request to help fund completion of a cannabis cultivation build-out in Phoenix.
- [We are not a free salesperson](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/we-are-not-a-free-salesperson/): NuWay wanted a new U.S.
- [What 2008 actually taught me](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/what-2008-actually-taught-me/): I built Tellus into a real design-build firm in Southern California, and then 2008 happened.
- [Whose Number Is It, Really](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/whose-number-is-it-really/): As Common Ground's public sites, wiki pages and resume materials multiplied, small factual drifts started compounding.
- [Zero red lines, never our own stamp](https://wiki.commonground.ventures/stories/zero-red-lines-never-our-own-stamp/): I set a specific quality bar for the virtual architecture bench we were building, structural, mechanical, civil, plumbing, HVAC, fire, landscape, jurisdictional review, all feeding into the plans our system produced.
